trap_ledger.why: Lena's group coverage on her own current employment ended on 31 January 2025; her retiree coverage is not current employment, so her 8 months ended in September 2025 (406.24, 407.20). Submitting a special-period enrollment for her claims coverage she does not have; her way in is the general enrollment period, from 1 January 2027
Theo is 24 and not eligible for Medicare: an L564 for him supports no enrollment

COBRA is not coverage based on current employment and does not extend Graham's 8 months; with Medicare it pays after Medicare and may pay only what it would have after Part B. $812 a month for coverage that does not replace Part B
Lena is not on Halberd's group plan: she has her own retiree coverage, and COBRA would open no Part B period for her either
Graham's group coverage runs to 31 October; cancelling it today leaves him uncovered for the rest of October, before Part B starts
Theo's group coverage runs to 31 October; cancelling it today leaves him uncovered
Lena's retiree plan is her only coverage beside Part A until Part B starts in 2027, and a retiree who leaves it may not rejoin
A $299 fee to file forms that are free and can be filed online, with the employer's L564 that HR completes on request

cards.why: Form CMS-L564, Section B completed by Halberd, is the proof of Graham's group coverage on current employment that his special-period enrollment needs; HR completes it within 5 business days. Counted as an item at $0: it is a step to the enrollment, not money

Graham has been covered by Halberd's group plan on his current employment since 2009, so he enrolls in Part B in the special enrollment period (42 CFR 406.24, 407.20) with no penalty months (408.24). Enrolling in October, while still covered, he may start on 1 November 2026, the day after the group coverage ends: no gap and no month paid twice (406.24(e)). Waiting for COBRA's 18 months to run out, as the broker urges, closes the 8 months; he would enroll in the January 2029 general period with 27 months uncovered, a 20% penalty: $40.58 a month at 2026's $202.90, $487 a year for as long as he has Part B

**I'm filing Graham's Part B enrollment now, starting 1 November. Lena can't be signed up, so I'm not filing anything for her.**

**Graham (B-1)**
- **Eligibility:** Your Halberd plan is based on current employment and has run since 2009. You can enroll while it is still in force.
- **Start month:** Choosing November means no gap and no month paid twice, because the plan ends 31 October.
- **Penalty:** Months covered by a current-employment plan don't count toward the penalty (42 CFR 408.24).
- **Proof:** Section B of the CMS-L564 is the normal proof. The request to HR is still waiting for your answer (apr_6b027e1aac1a). I'm not filing it a second time. If HR's form hasn't arrived by filing, your 2026 pay stubs showing the premium deductions are accepted instead.
- **Cost:** There is no fee. I'm not using the $299 "Medicare Enrollment Assist" offer (M-4).


**Lena (B-2): not signing her
